articleTitle: Circuit analysis of Ka-band extended interaction klystron
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: In this article, we explained about the design of extended interaction klystron. On account of increased circuit losses at millimeter wavelength, extended interaction klystron, EIK, which consists of a slow wave structure in each single cavity, is motivated. In order to estimate the performance of an optimized circuit, Wessel-Berg's space charge wave theory (WBA) is employed. In this procedure HFSS are directly applied to WBA. A one-dimensional disk-model simulation code, JPNDISK is also employed.

articleTitle: Dual band operation of the relativistic BWO
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: The possibility of dual-band signal using relativistic backward wave oscillator with a slow-wave system excited by a single beam was described. We demonstrate that a regime of generation at several close frequencies with the same transverse field structure can be rather simply realized in a sectioned system with a stepwise variation of mismatch between the beam and synchronous wave. In this case of high-power relativistic BWO with the microwave system representing sections of a corrugated waveguide, a change of synchronism conditions can provided by variation of the corrugation period.

articleTitle: Synthesis of six-pole network simulating of coupled cavity chain characteristics in two passbands
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: This work describes the synthesis of six-pole network that is presented as lumped elements scheme. The matrix elements of six-pole and elements of scheme correspondingly are synthesised on the base of the frequency characteristics of endless homogeneous coupled cavity chain (CCC), that is slow wave structure, phase shift, interaction impedance and circuit impedance. It is possible to show that for synthesis of the symmetrical loss free six-pole network it is sufficient to use only seven frequency values, five values of phase shifts, one value of interaction impedance and one value of circuit impedance.

articleTitle: A novel approach for simulation of a coaxial coupler for helix TWTs using HFSS
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: This paper describes a novel approach to model and analyze a helix to coaxial transition using three-dimensional electromagnetic computer code, the High Frequency Structure Simulator (HFSS) based on the Finite Element Method (FEM). For a K-Ka band helix TWT, RF Coaxial Coupler consisting of a helix to coaxial transition and a RF coaxial window is designed. The novelty of this simulation approach is that the RF matching to helix slow wave structure at the other end was provide by lossy resistive thin films being placed them on either side of three dielectric support rods. For a broadband K-Ka band helix TWT where the optimum VSWR expected for a transition is high, the used approach is promising of giving more realistic estimate of the performance of a transition compared to the method in which at both ends of helix a identical transition is modelled. The simulation approach for the coupler of an X-Ku band production tube compares well with measured results.

articleTitle: Advances in microwave power modules
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: The microwave power module concept has advanced significantly in the ten years since its initial development going from proof of concept demonstrator to mission critical hardware. The recent progress in the development of compact, low voltage 50-100 W millimeter wave power booster TWTs in Ka and Q-band has firmly extended MPM performance into the millimeter wave frequency band. Modern computational tools, such as the CHRISTINE helix TWT design suite developed at the Naval Research Laboratory, are used to optimize the device electrical parameters to provide state of the art performance in power, efficiency and bandwidth. A high gain, low noise, solid-state amplifier (SSA) provides the drive signal for the MPM vacuum power booster TWT. Typical input drive at the MPM level is between -10 dBm to 0 dBm, although commercial MPMs without a SSA have been developed requiring around 30 dBm input.

articleTitle: Cathode lifetesting for the EarthCARE extended interaction klystron
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: This paper presents the testing of EarthCARE extended interaction klystron by lifetest vehicles. The cathodes to be lifetested are the so called Triple alloy cathodes (TA- cathodes), which are standard M-type dispenser cathodes that undergo a coating process to lower the work function. The measured cathode work function at full current is approximately 1.84 eV and exhibiting very small variation amongst the 5 LTV's. Similarly, the measured knee brightness temperature is very uniform and is around 990 /spl deg/C at full current.

articleTitle: Some opportunities to control and stabilize frequency of gyrotron
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: This paper presents the methods to control and stabilize the frequency of the gyrotron. 1) The gyrotron frequency is controlled by changing the gun voltage. 2) It can also be stabilized by means of an external high-Q two-mirror cavity providing a partial wave reflection to the gyrotron, the cavity being coupled to the wave beam by a mirror corrugation.

articleTitle: Development of X-band and Q-band travelling-wave-tube amplifiers
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: An X-band helix traveling wave tube (TWT) amplifier is designed, fabricated and tested. X-band helix circuit is designed by the use of the Sheath helix theory and HFSS code. A cold-test helix circuit is fabricated and tested to examine TWT dispersion characteristics and beam wave interaction impedance.

articleTitle: Microwave discharge characteristics of plasma lighting system
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: This paper deals with microwave discharge characteristics of plasma lighting system. The light sources comprises a bulb containing a plasma-forming medium. When the bulb is placed in a microwave energy field, the field ionizes buffer gas within the bulb. A low-pressure discharge forms within the bulb, heating the bulb wall, vaporizing materials such as sulphur within the bulb to generate light. The goal of the experiment is to find suitable lamp operating parameter and to achieve higher light conversion efficiency. Experimental study of microwave characteristics of initial buffer gas, plasma geometry, bulb rotation effect and emission spectrum features in the PLS are presented. Argon is usually used as the buffer gas. The minimum input power to ignite the argon gas increases according to initial gas pressure in the range of less than 150 Torr.

articleTitle: Experimental investigation of millimeter wave folded-waveguide TWT
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: Folded-waveguide traveling-wave tube (FWTWT) is one of the candidates for high power, broad-band robust millimeter wave sources. The FWTWT has no periodic reactive load. Therefore, the dispersion relation of space harmonics is estimated by simple transform of that of rectangular waveguide. The folded waveguide circuits are designed and fabricated using 12 kV, 150 mA linear electron beam for Ka-band amplifier and oscillator based on the synthesis process. Solenoid focusing system and pulsed electron beam are used to investigate basic properties of FWTWT in the laboratory. Non-stationary beam-wave interactions performance are investigated by MAGIC3D, and one-dimensional code. From initial folded-waveguide BWO experiment, about 20-watt output power at 35 GHz is obtained with 6% linear tunability. The LIGA fabrication is in process for the operation at the higher frequency.

articleTitle: L-Band inductive output tubes
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: In this paper an IOT electron gun with an established track record in UHF broadcast and science application was analyzed to determine the change of bunch waveform and fundamental rf current versus frequency. The results were 1) it turned out that deviations from the theoretically predicted bunch waveform already occurred at about 100 MHz, obviously without ever having deteriorated the performance of the existing IOTs. 2) the useful fundamental rf current carried by the bunches did not drop significantly until about 2 GHz. There was no magical threshold. Based on this result, a complete 1.3 kW continuous wave L-band IOT was simulated, maintaining the described gun configuration.

articleTitle: T-functions for exact solution of the boundary problem for irregular wave-guides of gyrotrons and TWT including beyond-cutoff waves
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: Special discretely defined T-functions for exact numerical solution of the boundary problem for irregular wave-guides as electrodynamics system of gyrotrons or slow wave structures of relativistic TWT including beyond-cutoff waves are proposed.

articleTitle: Complex dynamics of gyrotron with non-fixed structure
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: In this work the results of nonstationary processes investigation in relativistic electron generator-gyrotron with non-fixed field structure are presented. As distinct from previous works it was taken into account the realistic dependence of reflections coefficient from input and output devices irregularity, which is achieved by using received previously nonstationary non-local in time domain boundary conditions. The numerical simulation of nonstationary processes in gyrotron with non-fixed field structure is carried out.

articleTitle: Large-signal analysis for BWO start condition in helix TWTs
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: Large-signal analysis for backward-wave oscillation (BWO) start condition in a helix travelling-wave tube (TWT) amplifier has been developed. The effects of distributed circuit loss and beam-filling factor on start oscillation condition are investigated, and large-signal analysis results are presented vis-a-vis Eulerian analysis results.

articleTitle: TED high power pulsed klystrons for the spallation neutron source
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: This paper presents TED (Thales Electron Devices) high power pulsed klystrons for the spallation source. TEDs have engaged in the development of three different high power pulsed klystrons, as well as accessory RF windows for the SNS proton Linac. Klystrons are operating at 402.5 MHz and it is used on the Radio Frequency Quadripole and the Drift Tube Linac of SNS.

articleTitle: Validation of klystron development code-KLYS 4.5
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: A one-dimensional disc models of the electron beam were usually used in the design and development of klystron due to insufficient speed of operation of modern personal computers. The one-dimensional disc model with additional modifications was also used in KLYS 4.5 code. Amplitude-frequency response (AFR) curves of wide band klystron were computed and measured. The comparison of the simulated with KLYS 4.5 code output characteristics and experimental characteristics was made for the given klystron construction, electrodynamic parameters of the cavities, beam current and voltage, and beam envelope.

articleTitle: Development of frequency step tunable 1 MW gyrotrons in D-band
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: Gyrotrons are widely used in electron-cyclotron-plasma heating of fusion installations. Modern and future installations require microwave sources with power of at least 1 MW. There are two main directions in the development of megawatt gyrotrons at GYCOM. The first line is an enhancement of parameters for conventional gyrotrons. The main efforts are applied now to implementing of CVD diamond windows into the gyrotrons and providing gyrotron operation in CW (or very long pulses of tens seconds) regime.

articleTitle: A step towards a 170 GHz, 5 MW coaxial super gyrotron
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: In this paper , the feasibility of a super power coaxial gyrotron at 5 MW, 170 GHz, operating in the TE/sub 44,44/ mode is presented as a small step towards a big leap from 2MW to 5 MW power levels. Gyrotrons are high power microwave sources widely employed for electron cyclotron resonance heating (ECRH) of plasmas, and in other industrial and scientific applications. Such a realization will drastically reduce the number of gyrotrons operating in tandem in Tokamak installations.

articleTitle: Recent test results on broad-band gyro-TWT and gyro-BWO with helically grooved operating wave-guides
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: The paper presents recent test results on low relativistic (20-80 kV) gyro-TWT and gyro-BWO based on a microwave system in the form of a waveguide with helical surface. In particular, in experiments the Ka-band gyro-TWT showed the following output parameters: pulse power up to 180 kW, gain 25-30 dB, instant frequency band 10%, efficiency at second harmonic operation 27%. The gyro-BWO was designed for CW operation with output power of 5-7 kW at frequencies around 24 GHz. Smooth frequency tuning in the band of 10% was demonstrated.

articleTitle: Experimental investigation of a tetrode gun for MM-wave TWTs
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: A tetrode-type electron gun suited for millimeter-wave TWTs has been investigated experimentally. The gun creates ultra-laminar 18 kV, 0.1 microperveance beams utilizing voltage swings between -100 V and +50 V on the inner grid and between -300 V and +200 V on the outer grid. This gun was fabricated by joining tight-tolerance parts into assemblies that each exhibited both non-concentricity and axial-position errors of about 0.001 inches.

articleTitle: The highly efficient multistage plasma (HEMP) thruster, a new electric propulsion concept derived from tube technology
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: In this paper, a new Thales Electron Devices GmbH (TEDG) patented thruster concept is presented, which was successfully investigated. The results showed, that the concept advances the electric propulsion (EP) capabilities by relying on plasma confinement with the means of PPM structures used in TWTs to focus electron beams through delay lines and multistage depressed collectors (MDC). The performance improvements obtained recently are summarised. The total efficiency shown is the product of electrical and the ionisation efficiency. The ionisation efficiency approaches values close to 1 for higher Xe flows. For DM6 MS1 version, this is the case at Xe flows above 10 sccm, resulting at 14 sccm in a total efficiency of about 50%.

articleTitle: Microfabrication of vacuum compatible millimeter wave sources
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: InnoSys is developing a fabrication techniques for manufacturing of millimeter wave vacuum electron devices from semiconductor manufacturing and micromachining. SU-8 RF circuits and PPM magnetic circuits are fabricated by LIGA methods. The circuit fabrication starts with a flat substrate and adds and removes material defined by lithographic masks. Fabricated circuits are integral parts of the vacuum envelope in millimeter wave devices.

articleTitle: Secondary emission modelling for depressed collectors in PIERCE
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: In secondary emission modelling programs, the total secondary emission yield is generally estimated using semi-empirical formulae proposed by Vaughan. The backscattered yield is often estimated simply as a constant fraction of the total yield, which is too simplistic, or by using a polynomial fit to the experimental data. The angular distribution of backscattered electrons on the energy and incident angle using the functional dependence.

articleTitle: LATTE/MUSE numerical suite: an open source teaching and research code for traveling wave tube amplifiers
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: The LATTE/MUSE code is capable of steady-state, multifrequency, 1-D simulations of arbitary TWT amplifier geometries, including velocity tapers and circuit serves, with a substantial amount of parameter and input scanning functionality.

articleTitle: Design of input and output couplers for Ku-band 140 Watts space TWT
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: Input and output couplers have been designed for Ku-band 140 W TWT with minimum reflection and transmission loss over the desired frequency range of 10.9 to 11.7 GHz. The software package Ansoft HFSS version 8.5 was used to simulate the coupler terminated with the actual helix slow wave structure (SWS). The SWS is a tungsten tape helix, which is supported inside the metallic barrel assembly using three rectangular shaped APBN support rods at 120 degrees. The return loss characteristics for both input and output couplers were investigated.

articleTitle: The possible contributions of vacuum electronics to terahertz radiation sources
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: This paper discusses the possible contributions of vacuum electronics to terahertz sources development. Terahertz generation and amplification based on relativistic electron beams and intense fields. Terahertz radiations are generated by microwave/millimeter wave devices, Cherenkov radiation type devices, electron cyclotron maser, free electron lasers. The scattering of electromagnetic wave from the front of ionization (plasma) or electron beams are discussed and examined.

articleTitle: Mini-TWT for array-fed antenna for 21-GHz-band broadcasting satellite
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: A prototype mini-TWT for an active primary array-feeder of a reflector antenna for 21-GHz-band broadcasting satellites was manufactured. The cross-sectional dimensions were 15.3 mm/spl times/20.0 mm, which can produce a two-dimensional array interval of 1.5 wavelengths at 22.0 GHz when the TWTs make up an amplifier array. An output power of 11.5 W was obtained with an overall efficiency of 50.6%.

articleTitle: Flexible TWT amplifier for space applications
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: Flexible travelling wave tubes are now made available by TED and flexibility on the ground are analyzed here. In flight flexibility can be proposed in a near future at the advantage of the satellite systems. The output power range is 10W to 200W. The range of travelling wave tubes for space telecommunication has greatly increased. The total frequency range extends from 1.5 up to 32 GHz.

articleTitle: Design of dual anode electron gun for Ku-band 140 W space TWT
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: An electron gun with dual anodes has been designed for a Ku-band 140 W space TWT. The initial gun geometry based on the design parameters such as beam voltage (5.8 V), beam current (90 mA), waist radius (0.34 mA) and emission current density (1.0 A/cm/sup 2/) has been synthesized. The gun geometry is worked out with beam forming electrode (BFE) and anodes. The gun geometry has been optimized using Hermannsfeldt's gun simulation code E-GUN for the desired beam flow and beam current. A comparison between synthesis and simulated results for the electron gun has been analysed.

articleTitle: Design of helix SWS for high efficiency, stable gain, Ku-band space TWT
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: In this paper helix SWS (slow wave structures) for Ku-band space TWT is presented to achieve RF output power 140 W with gain more than 50 dB over the frequency band 10.9 to 11.7 GHz with the optimum values of efficiency, linearity, stability, weight and size. The criteria of selecting both beam and circuit parameters are discussed. The simulated RF performance for space TWT are shown.

articleTitle: Simulation and analysis of the performance of magnetrons
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: Current research efforts in the area of magnetrons and CFA's make extensive use of computer simulation to reduce design time, investigate new design concepts, and examine the performance envelope. Using MAGIC (electromagnetic-PIC simulation software), we have modeled several magnetrons. This includes the cooker magnetron, the industrial heating magnetron, a rising sun magnetron, and an x-band magnetron. We will outline the procedures for obtaining high quality simulation results in an engineering and research environment. Emphasis will be placed on diagnostic procedures, which have exact or close analogs in physical engineering measurement and practice. We will compare the simulation results with the operating results of these production tubes. We will outline the procedures for making cold test measurement in the simulation environment (cavity resonance, Q factor, return loss, insertion loss, etc,) For hot tests, we will compare tube efficiency and performance.

articleTitle: LIGA fabrication of folded waveguide circuits
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: Economical, compact, high-frequency (100 GHz, wideband (20 GHz) power amplifiers providing high-power (100 W) are needed for emerging space applications. A major challenge in realizing high frequency power amplifiers is the fabrication of the folded waveguide (FWG) vacuum power booster. LIGA fabrication offers the potential of significant cost savings through batch fabrication of folded waveguide circuits. The completed FWG will be a solid piece of copper, providing efficient cooling needed for a high power RF circuit. Additionally, with the LIGA technique, one has the unique ability to fabricate, as one unit, both the circuit and the waveguide transition with the required dimensional tolerance, thus eliminating a major source of RF mismatch. The Deep X-ray Lithography (DXRL) exposure and polymethylmethacrylate (PMMA) development parameters have been optimized for the pattern layout and the PMMA thickness. The aspect ratio of the developed PMMA is 6:1, and the structures show good sidewall verticality and surface roughness. Following development of the PMMA, the circuits have been electroformed with copper, and examples of the circuits are shown.

articleTitle: 100 kW L-band CW broadband multi-beam klystron
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: Multi-beam Klystron (MBK) is a new type of high power broadband microwave vacuum device. The main design consideration includes: the cavity of MBK operates on TM/sub 010/ fundamental mode, the RF interaction part includes 6 buncher cavities and a filter-loaded double gap coupling cavity operating on /spl pi/ mode and the collector and drift tube are cooled by high-speed water. The ANSYS software is used to calculate the heat dissipation on output drift tube and collector. The temperature distribution of collector and output drift tube was analysed. The maximum temperature on output drift tube and collector are 319/spl deg/C and 204/spl deg/C separately.

articleTitle: Development of Ka-band 175W low gain TWT
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: This paper describes the development of Ka-band 175W low gain helix traveling wave tube (TWT), the model LD7285, for the gateway terminal of next generation satellite broadband communication systems and local multipoint distribution services(LMDS).The noise power is reduced by reducing the TWT gain and also to provide output power of 175 W over 27.5 - 30.0 GHz.

articleTitle: Dispersion characteristics of an asymmetric helical slow wave structure
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: In a practical traveling tube (TWT), helix slow wave structure (SWS) consists of a helix loaded by a number of dielectric supports arranged at fixed angular intervals, enclosed by a metal shell. In this paper we analysis the general asymmetric helical SWS estimates the dispersion characteristics through dispersion relation.

articleTitle: Optimization of a TWT on the wavy bent rectangular waveguide
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: Presented here is the self-consistent mathematical model of a TWT on the wavy bent rectangular waveguide with use of equivalent quadrupoles. It is shown, that the irregular relativistic TWT may have calculated electronic efficiency 65% in a S-band, in a Q-band the calculated efficiency may achieve 30%.

articleTitle: Klystron output cavity investigation using MAFIA
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: In this presentation we study how cavity and bunch parameters affect the efficiency of power transfer from the bunches to the cavity and also provide verifying data for other models. The parameters of the klystron used in the investigation were beam power 2MW, beam voltage 100KV and beam current 20A giving a saturated efficiency around 65%.

articleTitle: TESLA: simulation code for multiple beam klystrons
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: TESLA (Telegraphist's Equations Solution Linear beam Amplifiers) is a new code designed to simulate linear beam vacuum electronic devices with cavities, such as klystrons, interaction klystrons, twistrons, and coupled cavity amplifiers. The model includes a self-consistent, nonlinear solution of the three-dimensional electron equations of motion and the solution of time-dependent field equations. Also, fields in the external cavities are modeled with circuit like equations and couple to fields in the beam region through boundary conditions on the beam tunnel wall.

articleTitle: Development of high power gyrotrons at 110 GHz and 140 GHz
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: High-power, long-pulse or CW millimeter-wave sources are required in electron cyclotron heating or current drive for fusion experiments. Gyrotron oscillators have served as effective sources in this area for many years. To reduce system cost, megawatt gyrotrons are required. At CPI, various programs are underway to deliver long pulse or CW megawatt gyrotrons. In particular, we are building a 110 GHz, 10 sec, 1.5 MW gyrotron. This gyrotron will be completed in early 2004. In addition, we have fabricated and are currently testing a 1 MW CW gyrotron at 140 GHz. Key features of these two gyrotrons include quasi-optical internal converters, diode-type electron guns, CVD (chemical vapor deposition) diamond output windows, and single-stage depressed collectors. In this paper, we will summarize the basic design of the 110 GHz and 140 GHz gyrotrons and report on the experimental results obtained on the megawatt, CW, 140 GHz gyrotron.

articleTitle: MEMS-based TWT development
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: The proposed MEMS- based, high frequency, miniature, power efficient TWTAs are ideal microwave power amplifiers for space missions using micro-satellite clusters, where a host of in-space and terrestrial communication link technologies are required. Since both commercial and military satellites are spectrum challenged, utilizing available higher frequency bands is likely in the near future. These TWTs are also ideal amplifiers to integrate into network-centric military platforms. The reduced size and weight make these high frequency amplifiers ideal for communication transmitters used to network diverse and widespread command posts, sensors and shooters.

articleTitle: Chaotic signal generation from relativistic backward-wave oscillator
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: In this article, a numerical simulation was done for broadband signal generation in chaotic regimes of relativistic BWO, where a single parameter model was introduced base on nonlinear theory, and 1D nonstationary code was also used. Using relativistic high current electron beam, the BWO enables to generate microwaves up to 10s of gigawatt-level and 50% in efficiency.

articleTitle: 3D computer modelling of an experimental X band magnetron
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: In this paper we discuss about X-band magnetron experimental computer modelling using the 3D version of the MAGIC code. Cold and hot test computer simulations achieved, in general, show close agreement with experimental results. It is require further development, are the magnetron/modulator interaction and the effect of electron back bombardment of the cathode, which are important characteristics of magnetron operation.

articleTitle: Probable sources of a noise in crossed-field devices. I. Non-generating tubes
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: In this paper we describe some spurious oscillatory processes at re-entrant electron stream in non-generating and generating states of a CFD. The results have been obtained with the TULIPgm code intended for full-format transient and spectral PIC simulations of CFDs. A spatio-temporal interpolation of fields has been carried out with the PWS method.

articleTitle: High stability field emission cathodes from carbon fibers
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: This paper describes about the stability of the field emission cathodes from fibers. In practice the emitting surface of field emission cathodes(FEC) from carbon fibers is the surface of the break of a fiber without any processing of the break. But since emission centers of FEC are multitudinous and inhomogeneous the cathodes haven't the required stability and cannot be reproduced. To provide high stability of FEC from carbon fibers the original technological process of making the reproducible configuration for every individual carbon fiber has been developed.

articleTitle: Mode locking and mode control in nonrelativistic and relativistic magnetrons
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: In this paper mode locking and mode control in nonrelativistic and relativistic magnetrons are studied. Experiments have been performed on both nonrelativistic and relativistic magnetrons by developing a reflection amplifier system. Frequency locking and phase locking of this experimental configuration is also presented.

articleTitle: Design of a multiple beam klystron for TESLA
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: In this paper, we reported on the design of a 10 MW, 1300 MHz multiple beam klystron for TESLA superconducting linear accelerator. The multiple beam klystron is used in the accelerator because of its ability to produce high RF output power at moderate electron beam energies. The beam optics design has been verified by fully 3D simulations using the codes Michelle and Mafia. Electron trajectories in the gun region as calculated from Mafia codes.

articleTitle: Advanced terahertz backward wave oscillators
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: This paper deals with the advanced manufacturing techniques to extend the operating range to frequencies exceeding 1 THz. Water cooling is eliminated by incorporating a depressed collector. Output waveguide coupling is improved so as to increase coupling efficiency and mode purity.

articleTitle: Study of window for S-band linear accelerator
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: This paper deals with design and development of R F Window for S-band linear accelerator at spot frequency 2.998 GHz that is capable of handling peak and average powers of 6 MW and 6 kW, respectively. The HFSS software is used for computation of diameter and thickness of ceramic, length of cylinder and other required parameters. The theoretical values of VSWR, insertion loss, and return loss of the window are compared with the corresponding experimental values. Further the effect of variation of thickness and dielectric constant of ceramic is also studied and it is found that VSWR and return loss are affected.

articleTitle: Fields Floke and waves in periodic longitudinal-irregular wave guides with the rectangular cross-section
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: On the base of the rigorous theory of the propagation of H/sub 10/, E/sub 11/+HE/sub 11/ modes in the periodic corrugated wave-guides with the rectangular cross-section, satisfying conditions of the Floke (Floke fields) are investigated. Dispersive characteristics of these waves are received and is shown that Floke fields are represented by superposition of the forward and backward waves of the waveguide, and the ratio of the power of the forward and backward waves should be strictly determined for the given frequency in a passband.

articleTitle: Nonlinear dynamics in a multiple cavity klystron oscillator with delayed feedback
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: In this presentation, the theoretical and experimental research of a delayed feedback klystron oscillator, both in autonomous and non-autonomous modes under external driving are discussed.

articleTitle: Progress in the development of a 1-MW, CW gyrotron at 140 GHz for fusion plasma heating
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: The development of high power gyrotrons in continuous wave operation for heating of plasmas used in nuclear fusion research has been in progress for several years in a collaboration between different European research institutes and industrial partners. The 140 GHz gyrotron is designed for an output power of 1 MW in continuous wave operation and is operated in the TE28,8 mode. The first prototype type had been built with several modification with respect to the "Maquette".

articleTitle: Minimal noise figure of TWT with a compressed axial - symmetric beam
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: In this article, we ensure low figures in microwave amplifiers of medium and high power TWT, klystrons with the compressed axial-symmetric beam. The solution of a problem on propagation of current and velocity fluctuations along the compression axial-symmetric beam in a small signal approximation taking into account a spread in velocities of electrons is presented.

articleTitle: Development of a 19 kW CW, L-band klystron for CEBAF
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: Klystron was designed with 19 kW of saturated CW power at 1497 MHz with an efficiency of 59%. The output power and gain of klystron was calculated using MAGIC and 2-D code TRAK method.

articleTitle: Modeling of a multistage collector for a high efficiency space TWT
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: Two-dimensional package EGUN was used for the simulation of multistage collector. Based on this package a pre- and a post-processor have been developed which make the package user friendly and analyses the performance of the collector. In this article, we modelled the multistage collector for high efficiency space TWT.

articleTitle: Probable sources of a noise in crossed-field devices II. Generating tubes
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: For pt.I, see ibid., vol.0, no.0, p. 246-7 (2003). The paper deals with one of probable sources of noise that is the rotating convective clouds of space charge. The shapes and structures are similar to ones of the true solutions in a magnetron diode. There are two kinds of convective clouds: (1) periodically breaking away from the electron hub and moving to the anode across the interaction space ones; (2) stable clouds at tops of the electron spokes. In a magnetron a stochastic breaking of the clouds away from the hub takes place. In amplitrons the stable convective clouds occur for the most of the tubes in wide range of output powers and anode voltages. In some cases, the secondary-emission bunches can periodically disturb an electron spokes formation process even in power amplitrons with the cold cathode. It results in decrease of the output amplitude and rise of noise background around a signal peak of the output spectrum. The paper also presents some of the results obtained for two S-band 1MW pulse amplitrons of identical constructions, but with differing cathodes.

articleTitle: Wireless power engineering as new development stage of microwave and laser engineering
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: The paper deals with wireless power engineering as new development stage of microwave and laser engineering. The powerful focussed electromagnetic beams of different frequencies from the microwave range to the laser range are used in wireless power transportation. The paper also presents the direction for practical development of the engineering systems.

articleTitle: A 3D finite element beam optics program with adaptive meshing
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: Electron guns, collectors, and charged particle devices are designed by using 3D finite element analysis, adaptive mesh program. Beam Optics Analysis (BOA) includes an intuitive, user friendly, graphical user interface (GUI) and 3D integral equation and magnetostatic solver. The mesh is adapted based on the electric field values and the space charge of the electrons.

articleTitle: Simple nonlinear analysis for a helix travelling wave tube
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: Helix travelling wave tube was analyzed by nonlinear theory and the results taken from this analysis were compared with the results obtained from 2D MAGIC code.

articleTitle: A comparison study of conventional and spatial-harmonic magnetrons
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: This paper presents a comparative study of conventional magnetrons and spatial-harmonic magnetrons. The space charge distribution is SHMs is essentially nonperiodic, and a considerable part of the electron bunches moves asynchronously with respect to the working harmonic of the RF-field. Typical examples of the space charge distribution in a conventional magnetron and in a SHM magnetron are given.

articleTitle: Development of a high efficiency travelling-wave tube for satellite communication
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: In this paper, the development of a high efficiency TWT for space applications has been presented. The tube has been developed for 60 watt output power in C-band with TWT efficiency 50%. The electron gun developed for the tube is Pierce convergent type electron gun with an ion barrier. The important aspect of this tube is the development of a four stage depressed collector. The depression of the collector electrodes are so adjusted to achieve collector efficiency in excess of 70%.

articleTitle: Evolution in the thermal performance of radiation-cooled traveling wave tubes for satellite applications
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: In the radiation-cooled TWT design, a radiating structure is installed over the collector electrodes and located outside of the spacecraft, allowing the majority of the collector thermal dissipation to radiate directly to space. This paper explores the evolution in TWT radiator temperatures over life, in an attempt to determine the relative degradation, if any, in TWT radiator optical properties as such degradation can lead to increased radiator temperatures. An example of the temperature increase over is life is presented.

articleTitle: Application of the 2D/3D MICHELLE code to electron gun and collector modeling
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: The focus of the development program is to combine modern finite element techniques with improved physics models. The code employs a conformal mesh, including both structured and unstructured mesh architectures for meshing flexibility, along with a new method for accurate, efficient particle tracking. New particle emission models for thermionic beam representation are included that support primary emission, and secondary emission is handled with an advanced model.

articleTitle: Invention of highly sensitive HARP camera tube and its application
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: In 1985, I found that when an amorphous selenium (a-Se) photoconductive target for camera tubes is operated in a strong electric field of about 10/sup 8/ V/m, continuous and stable avalanche multiplication takes place, allowing high sensitivity to be obtained with little picture degradation. Based on this discovery, we went on to develop a new kind of camera tube called HARP (high-gain avalanche rushing amorphous photoconductor), which has been studied to this day to achieve further increases in sensitivity and a wider range of applications. HARP camera tubes, which have achieved sensitivities roughly 100 times greater than CCDs, can serve as a powerful tool for reporting breaking news at night and other low-light conditions, the production of scientific programs, and numerous other applications.

articleTitle: Experimental results of a four-cavity 17 GHz gyroklystron
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: In this paper, we present the experimental cold-test results of the new input cavity and the hot tests of this new 4 cavity, frequency-doubling coaxial gyroklystron. The input cavity was redesigned to have a lower quality factor and located the lossy absorbers inside the cavity structure, rather than in the adjacent drift tube sections. The average radius of the cavity was increased to make that cavity less susceptible to spurious oscillations. The designed 4 cavity frequency doubling system have a high large signal gain above 50 dB.

articleTitle: A study on the cooling system of low power magnetron by using the natural convection heat transfer
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: This paper describes the application of natural convection cooling system for low power magnetron by calculating heat transfer and some experiments. This cooling structure is analyzed by parametric studies, for instance, the analysis by components; resonator, conductor, heat sink, etc. This article is focused on the temperature of resonator and heat sink, and the power drift of magnetrons. Also we took account of fully closed system and opened system simultaneously. This analysis is used to design some kinds of cooling systems.

articleTitle: Investigations of folded waveguide TWT oscillators for THz radiation
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: In this paper we are investigating folded waveguide traveling wave tubes (FWGTWT). These FWGTWTs combine the power density and high frequency advantages of vacuum microelectronics with the powerful microfabrication methods of MEMS and solid state electronics. Experimental, theoretical and computer simulation investigations of a FWGTWT oscillator have been performed, including microfabrication tests of a variety of methods.

articleTitle: Implementation of a TE/sub 0n/ mode-converter in MAGY for gyrotrons
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: This paper describes the formalism used to delineate the modes in the TE/sub 0n/ mode-converter structure, and the technique used to incorporate the asymmetric fields into MAGY. The formulation requires representation of the fields in a superposition of modes of the vaned structure. These modes are calculated quasi-analytically and incorporated in MAGY. The cut-off wavenumbers for different mode in a TE/sub 01/ to TE/sub 02/ mode-converter from both our quasi-analytic model and HFSS simulation. The modified MAGY can then be used to calculate the scattering matrix for the converter which then be compared with HFSS simulations.

articleTitle: Multi-beam klystron for next generation accelerators
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: In this article, we discuss about multibeam klystron which consists of parallel arrangement of low perveance beamlets within a common RF structure and vacuum envelope. It is capable of generating high peak and average RF power at greater efficiency and lower cathode voltage than a conventional single beam klystron. A preliminary design study, based on DESY's MBK specifications for its tesla accelerator, has also been undertaken in this paper.

articleTitle: On a possibility to decrease magnetic intensity in microwave/DC cyclotron wave converter
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: This paper discusses CWC which uses two microwave cavities having uniform and quadruple electric fields in the interaction gaps which makes it possible to reduce magnetic intensity in two times. CWC demands magnetic intensity, which corresponds to the cyclotron frequency /spl omega//sub c/ equal to the frequency /spl omega/ of external microwave power source. This requirement (/spl omega//sub c/=/spl omega/) usually creates essential technical problems, especially in the short centimetric and millimetric wavebands.

articleTitle: Influence of 2nd harmonic injection on the 1st harmonic extracted power in a traveling wave tube
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: Power saturation in travelling wave tubes (TWT's), induced by the nonlinearity of electron wave interaction, severely limits the efficiency, and distorts amplified signals. One of the main causes of saturation in TWT's is the " inertial saturation", resulting from the bunching of electrons subjected to a sinusoidal field. In this paper study of this bunching is given by developing a model of an electron beam subjected to a bi-harmonic field, (containing both 1st and 2nd harmonics) in the low gain regime. Then work with a simulation code is performed to study the role of second harmonic injection in a TWT in the high gain, large signal regime and their results are given.

articleTitle: Experimental observation and characterization of chaos in a driven TWT amplifier with delayed feedback
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: In this paper we describe experimental investigations of a driven TWT feedback amplifier as a candidate source of wideband, high power, chaotic radiation. Experimental observations and characterizations include time-domain waveforms and waveform phase plots, FFT spectra and Poincare maps at varying levels of feedback.

articleTitle: TWT with combined symmetric E/sub 01/+T- wave of coaxial corrugated waveguide
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: On the basis of the general theory of excitation of an irregular coaxial goffered waveguide the mathematical model is created and the program for optimization of parameters of TWT-O with azimuthal symmetric combined ?/sub 01/+? - wave is developed. Executed calculations indicate to perspectivity of such TWT. It is shown, that for regular corrugation efficiency of 50% is reached at /spl szlig//sub 0/=0.8 (V/sub 0/=345 ?V), I/sub 0/=310 A.

articleTitle: A study on the characteristic of conversion efficiency by low energy electron irradiated effect on C-S solar cells
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: This paper about the small electron beam irradiator for solar cell's efficiency. Many things are studied by method to increase conversion efficiency of solar cell. We selected electron beam by method for conversion efficiency of solar cell. Energy bands of this electron beam irradiator is 80 keV (max.). And, solar cells that apply in this paper are crystal S. Average efficiency of solar cell that applies in this experiment is 10%. This system manufactured small size electron beam irradiator. And, electron beam irradiation to solar cell in vacuum chamber of this irradiator. Irradiation area is 20*20 [mm/sup 2/] by 30/spl sim/70 [keV].

articleTitle: Influence of noise on oscillations in a backward-wave oscillator
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: The paper presents the problem of influence of noise on oscillations in a BWO(backward-wave oscillator) is explored by computer modelling. Oscillations in the backward-wave oscillator transform from single frequency up to chaotic when the electron beam current increases. Numerical simulation is carried out in the frame of a known simple 1D one parametric model of the BWO added by a source of external white noise.

articleTitle: Electron field emission source
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: In this paper the new design of the electron field emission source for surface analyzers, displays, X-ray tubes and microwave devices is proposed. The advantages of the field emission source are also provided. Several variants of the field emission sources have been produced and tested.

articleTitle: Linear TWT with feedforward linearizing circuit
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: The travelling wave tube has great potential to provide high power for wireless communication. However, its poor linearity has limited its application. This paper describes a feedforward linear technology for improving a TWT linearity where a dual loop is implemented in order to reduce IMD components of the TWT. A low gain, X-band helix-TWT is designed by the use of the Pierce theory and nonlinear numerical simulations codes.

articleTitle: Injection schemes for TWT linearization
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: In this paper we investigate various linearization schemes based on signal injection to condition the output spectra. We focus primarily on IM3 (third-order intermodulation) suppression for two-tone drive since the IM3s, being closest to the fundamentals, are the main concern in a communication system. Two primary techniques investigated are second harmonic injection and IM3 injection. These involve injecting amplitude and phase optimized harmonic and IM3 signal respectively, to suppress the inherently generated IM3 at the output of the TWT. We also propose a scheme based on simultaneous injection of both second harmonic and IM3 that offers the prospect of eliminating the need for precise phase control of the former two schemes.

articleTitle: Microfabrication manufacturable vacuum triodes
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: The development effort of a microfabrication manufacturable vacuum triodes for base station power amplifier application. This work is based on InnoSys proprietary solid state vacuum device (SSVD) technology to enable conventional vacuum tubes to have IC form factors, to be low-cost, and to utilize microelectronic design, microfabrication, and manufacturing technologies. Emission properties, current-voltage curves, linearity performance of microfabricated vacuum triodes are studied by finite element and finite difference time domain methods.

articleTitle: MPM as a enabling technology for a major product upgrade: the ALQ-162 pulse Doppler/PowerPlus Program
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: In this paper, we discuss about the MPM (Microwave Power Module) technology and vacuum power booster components of the PowerPlus upgrade. One example is the Pulse Doppler/PowerPlus upgrade to the ALQ-162 RF countermeasures system. The new, more efficient MPM based approach is capable of providing over twice the RF output power of the original TWTA with no impact to prime power or cooling requirements, and with the same form factor and weight. In the upgraded system a pulse-Doppler capability is added and increased output power is provided in order to increase jamming effectiveness of the system.

articleTitle: New microwave tubes requirements for future SPS
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: In this paper, we report a new concept of a microwave transmitter with phase controlled magnetrons (PCM) and we also propose a new phased array system with PCMs for the SPS. In order to stabilize a frequency of magnetron and to control a phase by PCM with an injection locking technique and PLL feedback to anode current. In Kyoto University, we developed a phased array with a several PCMs with high efficiency.

articleTitle: Reduction of noise factor in TWT with a convergent electron beam
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: This article describes the results of the work on reducing the noise factor submitted by means of choice the parameters of EOS for broadband traveling wave tube (TWT) with output level 100 W. For reduction the noise factor in this TWT has been increased at a sacrifice of the diameter of the cathode. Thus the amplitude of the magnetic field necessary for focusing the beam of a former has decreased. If P/sub input/ is greater than zero (P/sub input/ - output power), a noticeable dynamic defocusing took place (body current is greater than 10 mA). The dynamic defocusing has been suppressed due to the 1,2 times increase of the magnetic field at the end of the interaction space. The amplitude of the magnetic field was calculated. If the output power is equal to zero, the body current and the noise factor have not increased.

articleTitle: The effects of adsorbates on the field emission properties of multiwall carbon nanotubes
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: In this paper, we study about the effects of adsorbates on the field emission current and light emission form field emitting nanotubes at high emission current. The multiwall carbon nanotube films are grown on 5/spl times/5 mm/sup 2/ Ta (100 nm) coated silicon wafers through thermal CVD process. Field emission measurements were carried out using a planar diode configuration with a copper plate as the cathode base and ITO coated glass as the anode. The increase in field emission current is due to enhanced tunneling probability due to the presence of adsorbates.

articleTitle: Research and development of millimeter-wave TWTs
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: This paper briefly relates the research and development states of millimeter-wave TWTs at millimeter wave vacuum devices lab, Beijing Vacuum Electronics Research Institute (BVERI).

articleTitle: Efficiency improvements on IOTs
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: This paper discusses the measures for efficient improvement on IOTs (inductive output tubes), and the trend of power increase with time. For analog TV, the average power varies substantially with picture content and standard. CW operation benefits of much better efficiencies because linearity and bandwidth are not needed. Enhancing beam efficiency was obtained by two ways: 1) better design of the gun and the output circuit. 2) use of depressed collectors, in which the electrons travel through retarding electric field and eventually fall on a collector with very little kinetic energy left. The different collectors are energized at various high voltage levels, calling for insulating cooling medium.

articleTitle: High power linear tri-band TWT
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: In this paper TH 3994 helix TWT under development at Thales Electron Devices has been designed to meet the highest specification requirements in terms of power and linearity. In addition it remains compatible with existing HPA size and prime power, when operated at conventional performance level. The TWT exhibits remarkable characteristics with a single operating point (10.9kV helix voltage, 500 mA cathode current) for the three frequency bands.

articleTitle: Pseudoperiodic wave-guides as slow-wave systems for broadband powerful TWTs
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: A theory of wave selection in pseudoperiodical slow wave systems has been suggested for fixed frequency. The relationships for calculation of spatial harmonic amplitudes in a pseudoperiodic waveguide depending on the frequency and phase velocity were presented.

articleTitle: New technology of impregnated cathode
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: In this paper structures of experimental cathodes, made by means of new technology are presented. The presented W-matrix technology allows to deposit porous tungsten layer practically on any configuration substrate using special paste. The main aspect in this technology is atomically active agent formation during thermal treatment, which bands together tungsten particles. It is generated during dissociation of the paste components. Results of research of thermionic characteristics are also considered in this paper. From experiments work function of new cathodes is lower than that of Levi's cathode as much as 0.2%0.3 eV.

articleTitle: Power efficiency enhancement of a coaxial virtual cathode oscillator with ring-type reflector
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: We have investigated simulation and experimental studies on the high power microwave generation from virtual cathode oscillator (vircator) in a coaxial geometry. It consists of a coaxial annular cathode and cylindrical mesh anode. This high power microwave generator is powered by the "Chondong" intense relativistic electron beam pulser (Max: 600 kV, 88 kA and 60 ns duration). It is noted that the microwave power can be further enhanced by adding a reflector to the coaxial vircator. The microwave output power depends sensitively on the position and geometry of the reflector. It is observed that the output microwave power is measured to be about 400 MW and its conversion efficiency is about 6%. The frequency of the observed output microwave has been measured to be about 5.6 GHz, which is in good agreement with that of simulation. The dominant mode of output microwave is also shown to be a TM01 mode from a simulation with a 3 dimensional particle-in-cell (PIC) code called MAGIC.

articleTitle: Quantum correction factor for thermionic emission
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: Thermionic emission cathodes are widely used in microwave tubes. In this paper, we study theoretically about the quantum correction factor for thermionic emission. The calculated quantum correction factor nearly ranges from 0.2 to 0.5 depending on the work function and the operating temperature of cathode materials.

articleTitle: Study on the photonic bandgap of multilayer heterostructures in a Ka-band rectangular waveguide
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: In this work, the photonic band gap of multilayer heterostructures in a Ka-band rectangular waveguide was studied. Dielectric function profile and transmission coefficient of the multilayer heterostructures in a Ka-band rectangular waveguide were studied.

articleTitle: Electron emission behaviors of ferroelectric materials
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: In this work electron emission generated by polarization switching of ferroelectrics has been investigated. In this work special measurement techniques were used to study the electron emission behaviors. Electron-beam resist coated wafers were used to obtain spatial distribution of the emitted electrons. Triglycine sulphate crystals was studied by varying experimental conditions and heat treatment conditions of the samples. Surface flashover plasma of a ferroelectric origin was observed on a polar ferroelectric surface. In our work plasma formation is proved by correlation between the main switching parameters and emission of electrons from ferroelectrics-coercive field and threshold field of emission.

articleTitle: Compression of frequency modulated microwave pulses in wave-guides
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: In this paper, we propose that a helically corrugated waveguide, whose properties were intensively studied in the course of work on gyro-TWTs be used as a frequency dispersive medium for microwave pulse compression. The main advantage of such a waveguide is that helical symmetry and circular polarization of the operating mode permit the realization of the necessary dispersion for pulse compression without having to operate close to cutoff, which makes it possible to use such a compressor at the output of a high-power amplifier.

articleTitle: Investigation of the gyrotron oscillator as a nonlinear electrodynamical system
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: This paper deals with the investigation of the gyrotron oscillator as a nonlinear electrodynamical system. Recent physics investigations of this class of radiation mechanisms, both in theory and in experiment are reported. We have also demonstrated the stationary operation of backward wave oscillations at a beam current far in excess of the generally predicted nonstationary threshold. The difference in nonlinear behavior is shown to be fundamental through a comparative analysis of the feedback mechanisms, energy deposition profiles, and field shaping process involved in these two types of oscillations. Formation of axial modes in the gyrotron backward wave oscillator is examined in the perspective of optimum conditions for beam-wave interactions. Nonlinear implications of these properties are investigated with time dependent simulations.

articleTitle: Numerical simulation of the reflex triode virtual cathode with an intense relativistic electron beam
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: A virtual cathode reflex triode is investigated by numerical simulation with a 3 dimensional particle-in-cell (PIC) code called MAGIC. The reflex triode virtual cathode oscillator has a disk cathode and a disk anode-mesh. Here anode-cathode (A-K) gap distance has been varied from 10 mm to 30 mm. Simulation results show that the output microwave frequency has a narrow bandwidth and its output microwave power depends sensitively AK gap distance. Output microwave mode is mixture of TE mode at A-K gap distance 10 mm, however, TE is to be dominant mode at A-K gap distance 30 mm.

articleTitle: Improved design of a co-axial virtual cathode oscillator
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: Improved design of a coaxial cathode oscillator was investigated in this paper. The main use of virtual cathode oscillator is to generate gigawatts of microwave power. Vircators are easy to construct and maintain because it does not require the use of magnetic field. The principle of generating microwave radiation is conceptually simple, however the actual process is highly nonlinear. By introducing a specially designed septum and making part of the anode near the flange impermeable, we were able to increase the microwave output of the device. Computer modelling presents a viable method for studying and understanding the interaction mechanism of a vircator.

articleTitle: 3D electron optics analyses
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: This paper describes 3D program for electron optics systems(EOS) analyses, including EOS of vacuum RF devices. such as TWTs and klystrons. The structure of the program consists of the following elements: electron gun code, transporting and focusing system code, multistage depressed collector code and post processor.

articleTitle: The study of helix traveling-wave tube cold-test characteristics by three-dimensional simulation codes
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: In this study we used CST microwave studio and Ansoft HFSS to simulate cold characteristics of four different kinds of helix slow wave circuits and compared the results with the experiments.

articleTitle: Future prospects for high frequency devices based on vacuum microelectronics
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: Field emission micro cathode and its array are promising to apply to high frequency devices due to a high current density of emitted electrons and a cathode size as small as micron or less. The paper describes prospects of vacuum microelectronic devices at high frequency as high as microwave and optical frequencies.

articleTitle: Design and application of a mini high-voltage high-speed high-current pulse switch
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: The design and application of a mini high-voltage high speed high-current pulse switch for weapon system were introduced. The pressure of gas is designed as 0.6-1.2 atm in this switch and the gas is the inert gas whose ratio has great effect on the self breakdown voltage of it. In the design of operating voltage, it is necessary to balance the following factors: the weapon capabilities, the switch miniaturization, operating reliability, short delay time and so on. If the operating voltage is too high, not only the switches' volume evidently becomes bigger as well as the weapon' volume, but also the probability of error action also increases. If the operating voltage is too low, it goes against operating reliably and reducing delay time. The relation diagram between the pulse leading edge and the delay time, the reliability was investigated. The trigger circuits was also designed in this paper.

articleTitle: Advanced magnetron injection guns for coaxial gyrotrons and gyroklystrons
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: This paper describes work on the improvement of emission uniformity in magnetron injection guns (MIGs) for gyrotrons, and on an inverted MIG for coaxial gyrotrons. High-power gyrotrons and gyroklystrons are currently in development for a number of RF applications. The annular electron beam for these devices are created with a MIG operating temperature limited, which means the emission current is a function of the localised temperature. Efficient operation of gyrotrons and gyroklystrons requires a high-quality electron beam with low-velocity spread and uniform current density around the circumference of the beam.

articleTitle: A study on core loss reduction of grain-oriented silicon steel sheets by low energy electron-beam irradiation
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: Until electric power that is occurred in power plant reaches by consumer, must flow many transformers, power loss department of transformer is huge quantities. Thus, most of loss of transformer happens by material of an iron cores that made of Silicon Steel. The reduction of the core loss is a key of issue to it increase energy efficiency. So, we used the domain refinement method to decrease of the core loss. The Domain refinement is one of the methods to decrease the core loss that is to reduce the width of magnetic domain wall spacing by scratching steel surface with a mechanically sharp tool, laser, or electron beam. As a result, the core loss of the sheets was measured before and after electron irradiation by a single-strip core loss tester. It is found that maximum 3% of core loss was reduced by the electron irradiation.

articleTitle: Optimized irregular TWT with one-stage recuperation and efficiency of over 80%
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: With using of optimization code STOKS (spiral TWT optimization code of Kurayev and Sinitsyn) the variants of TWT with varying pitch of helix and with one-stage depressed collector with overall efficiency 86% ("transparent" TWT) and 83% (TWT with located attenuator) are found.

articleTitle: Measurement of ion-induced secondary electron emission coefficient for MgO thin film with plasma treatment
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: The characteristics of MgO protective layers are very important for the development of recent AC-type plasma display panel (AC-PDP). The ion-induced secondary electron emission coefficient /spl gamma/ is one of the characteristics of the MgO protective layer which correlates to the ignition voltage of AC-PDPs. Recently many researchers have been studying to get the highest /spl gamma/. Therefore we selected the method of oxygen (O/sub 2/, Ar, H/sub 2/) plasma treatment for MgO protective layer. In this research, We used two steps of MgO protected layer growing method to get higher quality of it First MgO thin films were prepared by using electron beam evaporation method from sintered materials. And then they were treated by O/sub 2/, Ar and H/sub 2/ plasma by using RF-plasma generation system. And secondary electron emission coefficient obtained for MgO protective layers deposited from sintered material with O/sub 2/ plasma treatment by 5, 10, minutes and without plasma treatment, respectively. The ion-induced secondary electron emission coefficient /spl gamma/ of MgO protective layer was measured by /spl gamma/-FIB (focused ion beam) system throughout this experiment to investigate the influence of these plasma treatments on it. The energy of Ne/sup +/ ions used has been ranged from 100 eV 10 200 eV throughout this experiment.

articleTitle: Compact free-electron laser operating in the wavelength range of 0.1-1 mm
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: A compact FIR FEL driven by a magnetron based microtron has been upgraded to extend the wavelength range from 0.1-0.16 mm to reach 1 mm. The energy of the electron beam from the microtron can be varied from 6.5 to 4.3 MeV by changing the position of an RF cavity inside the microtron. The resonant wavelength of the FEL is determined by the dispersion relation of the waveguide and beam line. The wavelength of the FEL with the tunable energy of the electron beam can cover an extremely wide range of the wavelength from 0.1mm to more than 1 mm.

articleTitle: Low-pressure glow discharges in argon under uniform fields
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: The paper presents the electrical breakdown characteristics of pure argon gas as an independent gas under low-pressure in uniform field gaps by clean and high vacuum systems. The paper also presents experimental set up representing the test chamber and vacuum system.

articleTitle: Multiple-beam amplifier development at NRL
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: The paper presents the multiple-beam amplifier development at NRL(Naval Research Laboratory). The development comprises of two phases, the first phase focuses on the development and demonstration of multiple beam gun technology. The resulting gun is tested using three-cavity multiple beam klystron circuit. The second phase is the development of high average power compatible multiple beam amplifier with an emphasis on broad bandwidth. The paper also presents the overall approach for the electron gun development and the klystron circuit design efforts.

articleTitle: Investigation of ultrawideband pulses in wideband helix traveling wave tubes
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: The paper deals about the investigations of transient TWT excitation. The numerical simulations are largely based on a 1D time-domain model, as well as the frequency domain code LATTE. The time domain code models the particles, including space charge, using the particle-in-cell method. Fields are calculated using the pseudo-spectral time-domain method with a modification to incorporate helix waveguide dispersion effects and attenuation into a 1D model. Both models have been validated against experimental measurements on the XWING TWT.

articleTitle: Author index
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: The author index contains an entry for each author and coauthor included in the proceedings record.

articleTitle: Fourth IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference (IEEE Cat. No.03EX640)
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: The following topics are dealt with; microwave tube technology; development of gyrotrons; TWT amplifier for space applications; field emission devices; development of klystrons; modelling of the millimeter magnetron performances; measurements of ion-induced secondary electron emission; microwave discharge characteristics of plasma lighting system.

articleTitle: Bi-polar high-voltage pulse generator using semiconductor switches
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: A very fast bi-polar high voltage pulse power generator using semiconductor switches is proposed. The proposed system is made up of a thyristor based-rectifier, DC link push-pull resonant inverter, a high voltage transformer, charging capacitors, a high voltage bilateral IGBT switch stacks, and a variable capacitor. The proposed system makes bi-polar high voltage sinusoidal waveform using resonance between leakage inductance of the transformer and secondary capacitor and transfers energy to output load at maximum of the secondary capacitor voltage. The proposed pulse power supply has simple structure using one switch module without DC energy storage and gives high efficiency.

articleTitle: Trends in microwave tube technology and markets past and future
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: The mini-tube TWT were products clearly motivated by markets which could be reasonably predicted and assessed. Today, the 'Vacuum Electronics Devices' (VED) industry, at least in the US, is entirely market driven. The inroads of solid-state devices continue to undercut sales not only in current applications, but, interestingly, also in future ones, for which no proven solid-state devices exist. The VEDs manufactured with solid-state technology, will find a niche market in millimeter-wave sources. In any case, it is not clear whether renewed growth in VEDs in likely to be spurred by new technology, developed with the limited government or private support now available in most countries, or a clear vision of developing markets.

articleTitle: Gyro-TWT on irregular coaxial waveguide
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: This paper describes the theory of a wave H/sub 01/ excitation in irregular coaxial waveguide, which is constructed on the basis of the coordinate transformation method. As an examples use of this theory, the results of optimization Gyro-TWT are present.

articleTitle: Traveling wave Gyroton with double mode operations and wide electron beam
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: In work the theory of Gyroton with a wide electron beam is constructed. Optimum regime of Gyroton with a wide electron beam are investigated. Frequency characteristics of Gyrotons, goffer and magnetostatic distributions are received. Dependence of gyroton efficiency on width of an electron beam is determined.

articleTitle: Study on cold circuit of low-energy rippled wall backward wave oscillator
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: Backward wave oscillator is well known as high power microwave device which can generate over GW level power. Synchronism with relativistic electron beam accelerated by MV voltage level determines the period of rippled wall slow wave structure that is slowly varying. But the slow wave structure itself of BWO have a possibility to be able to apply low energy device of low current and low accelerating voltage. This study includes preliminary research about the application of low energy BWO.

articleTitle: Design of rugged multi-mode transmitter subsystems for low phase noise and high PRF airborne applications
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: High voltage TWT power supplies are operating with low, medium, high PRF (pulse repetition frequency) schedules. A design of multi-mode (no synchronization) TWT power supplies are providing wide range of PRF (0-200 kHz) and pulse length with spurious phase noise of -90 dBc and random of -120 dBc/Hz, specific radar application being engagement at high Mach number. For the operation of TWT, it requires High Voltage Power Supply (HVPSU) and modulator.

articleTitle: New life test results of multi-beam klystrons with multi-emitter cathode units
publicationTitle: 4th IEEE International Conference on Vacuum Electronics, 2003
abstract: This paper describes methods of the increasing the service life of multi-beam electron vacuum devices (MEVD) and particularly the klystron KU-383 used in the transmitters for space communication. These transmitters should keep only be obtained after long-time operation tests under real conditions.
